newsitem.title: UK: Forward sale best for wheat farmers - HGCA analysis.
newsitem.headline: Forward sale best for wheat farmers - HGCA analysis.

text.p: A UK farmer with feed wheat to sell in mid-October would have achieved the best return by February by selling it forward for February delivery, according to comparisons made by the Home Grown Cereals Authority.
In an analysis in its Weekly Digest the farmer would have received 100.80 stg.
But if he had simply sold spot grain in mid October and received four months' interest on what he got for it, he would have received in total almost as much, 100.60 stg.
The HGCA noted that the premium for forward prices in October this year was lower than in previous years due to a lack of optimism over prices.
Storing the grain until mid-February and then selling it on the spot market would have yielded 90.80 stg.
If the farmer decided to store the grain and hedge the sale using the LIFFE wheat contract, he could have received a total of 99.20 stg, according to the HGCA's calculations.
"Holding the grain for a later sale and hedging this using futures has usually produced better returns than selling in October for spot delivery," the HGCA said.

But this season the physical market fell by further than futures prices and so the profit made by buying back a futures contract in February was not enough to make up the difference between physical market prices in October and February, the HGCA said.

"However, the benefit of hedging when grain is held for future sale is clearly shown this season, with the return from hedging over eight stg per tonne above the return for selling spot in February," he authority said.

The HGCA noted that the success of a particular strategy in one year, or even over a period of several years, does not mean that similar results will be achieved in any given year. It also pointed out that its analysis does not cover other strategies such as pool trading or the use of options.
